title: airlock readiness profile (readiness 1)
description: 1.29.0 C12 (docs/2026-11-06-SPEC-1.29.0.md §2.3 (iii), principle E25): a readiness profile, the file a world's `api.readiness` names. It lists the topics, services and actions an integration needs in that half's world, each with why. The half evaluates it read-only from its own graph and the rates it measures on its carried and retained lanes, reports `readiness[]` in its status and doctor, and gates nothing on it. Strict like the config: an unknown key refuses the file (`airlock check --readiness <file>`, the half at start, a reload). tf chains are not in version 1.

name.description: The profile's name: doctor names its items readiness.<name>.<item>.

topic.description: An exact topic name of the half's world.

service.description: An exact service name; present when the graph lists it with a server (where the RMW says).

action.description: An exact action name; present when its <name>/_action/send_goal service is served.

type.description: pkg/msg/Name for a topic, pkg/srv/Name for a service, pkg/action/Name for an action; present under another type reads untyped.

purpose.description: Why the integration needs it (doctor prints it).

min_hz.description: A topic only: the rate it must keep, measured on a lane the half carries or retains (slow under it, idle on a carried lazy lane nobody demands, unmeasured on a name it neither carries nor retains). A retained name's standing reader is drained every 100 ms, so it measures up to about 10 Hz.
